A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DIRECT study. Their main text, algorithms, equations, figures, dataset table and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite retitling and reformatting.

before.justification: Sections 5 and Appendix E report original DIRECT and baseline experiments using ResNet-18 and CLIP under class imbalance and label noise.

after.justification: V4 retains these original experiments and adds long-tail benchmark results and an ImageNet-LT class-frequency analysis.

M1.justification: DIRECT's two-phase procedure remains the same. However, v4 Algorithm 1 omits the explicit restriction that VReduce's candidate endpoints lie within the current [I,J], present in v3 Algorithm 2. The surrounding prose still describes shrinking the version space, leaving uncertain whether this changes the search domain or merely abbreviates the notation.

E1.justification: V4 adds full-class CIFAR-10LT and CIFAR-100LT evaluations under label noise, plus ImageNet-LT and iNaturalist evaluations. These substantially extend coverage beyond the retained merged-class imbalance settings and FMoW/iWildcam benchmarks, testing additional long-tail distributions and classification requirements.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in matched experiments. The added benchmarks and class-frequency analysis use subsets of previously evaluated methods, including Random, BADGE, GALAXY and margin/confidence sampling. No new comparison method is introduced.

E3.justification: New protocols include CIFAR-LT evaluations with 15% label corruption and budgets reaching 10,000 labels, ImageNet-LT/iNaturalist sweeps reaching 100,000/60,000 labels, and accuracy grouped into 100-class frequency bins. These are settings for added experiments; the stated training and evaluation procedures for retained experiments remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 5.3 and Figure 7 add an ImageNet-LT analysis comparing accuracy across class-frequency bins, examining whether gains concentrate in rare classes. Earlier noise-level sensitivity tests and minority-label collection analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Existing four-trial means and standard-error bands remain unchanged. However, the new ImageNet-LT/iNaturalist curves in Figure 16(c)-(d) and class-frequency bars in Figure 7 lack uncertainty displays and corresponding run-count disclosures, making reporting less consistent. This does not establish that fewer runs were performed.

E6.justification: V4 adds learning curves for four long-tail benchmarks and class-frequency accuracy results. For example, Figure 7 reports 0.57 for DIRECT, 0.56 for Margin Sampling and 0.51 for Random Sampling on classes 901-1000. Earlier plotted results are retained unchanged; these additions do not represent same-setting performance improvements over v3.

T1.justification: Appendix C adds complexity expressions for additional methods, including CORESET, SIMILAR, Cluster Margin and BASE. Section 4.2 adds a conditional-noise formulation and assertions about optimality and preservation of guarantees under batching, without new supporting proofs. The existing threshold definitions and Appendix A-B proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a one-dimensional agnostic-learning reduction, parallel annotation under imbalance and noise, and annotation savings exceeding 60% against existing methods and 80% against random sampling. The revised title and increased dataset counts do not redefine these central contributions.

C2.justification: Section 5.3 newly attributes ImageNet-LT's overall advantage to improvements on less frequent classes despite modest losses on frequent classes. Section 4.2 expands the explanation of noise handling and inherited guarantees. Earlier limitations and the impact statement are retained, with the latter relocated.

D1.justification: Section 5 newly provides a direct public implementation link. Existing hardware, runtime, optimizer, pretraining, loss-weighting and label-smoothing disclosures remain unchanged. Appendix D briefly mentions the added CIFAR-LT variants, but Table 1 is not expanded to document the new datasets.

R1.justification: V4 adds Xie et al. (2024), Deep Active Learning in the Open World, to the imbalance discussion and Van Horn et al. (2018) for iNaturalist. The established positioning relative to GALAXY and ACED largely remains, with expanded discussion of inherited theoretical guarantees.

P1.justification: The title and abstract are rewritten, the method discussion gains a separate explanatory Section 4.2, and VReduce is presented before DIRECT. The impact statement moves from Appendix F to after the conclusion. Most retained prose and the overall narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The main text changes from a single-column preprint to a two-column conference layout, extensively resizing and relocating displays. Algorithms appear side by side, Figure 2's panels become vertically arranged, and the LabelBench figure expands to four panels. New class-frequency and CIFAR-LT displays accompany the retained plots.

improvement.justification: Broader full-class long-tail evaluation, the class-frequency breakdown in Figure 7, and a concrete implementation link improve empirical support and usability. The gain is limited by incomplete setup and uncertainty documentation for the new large datasets, stronger theoretical assertions without added proofs, and the ambiguous VReduce pseudocode edit.
